cons.claim: Visible effort creates the impression that the advisor controls outcomes they do not control, and the client's disappointment attaches to the advisor rather than the carrier
cons.example: a client who blames the advisor for a hotel category the operator substituted under a contractual right

failure_modes: improvising a fix and buying replacement services before establishing what the responsible party owes
letting the traveler accept the first offer without knowing what it forecloses
going quiet while working, so the client escalates emotionally
handling everything by phone and leaving no timestamped record for the claim afterwards
acceptance_tests: each incident has a log with timestamps, the contractual owner of the fix, actions attempted, names and supplier responses, and the notification cadence actually met
the file shows the client was told plainly which parts of the situation were outside the advisor's control
revisit_triggers: a disruption is resolved, which should trigger a review of what the protocol handled badly
a supplier's escalation path fails during a live incident
the same failure class recurs across clients

base.update_signal: a live incident exposes a step that made things worse, or a supplier escalation route that no longer works

nodes.definition: Pursuing remedy after a documented service failure - a category not delivered, a cancelled excursion, a substituted property, a transfer that never arrived - without ever promising the client an outcome. The advisor assembles the evidence trail already built by reconciliation and the incident log, files with the supplier through its own claims channel with a specific and proportionate ask rather than a general complaint, escalates factually up the relationship path when the first response is inadequate, and keeps the client informed about what is realistically available: a partial refund, a credit, a goodwill gesture, or sometimes nothing. Part of the skill is routing correctly - some failures belong to a carrier's own compensation regime and some to a protection policy's claims process, which the client pursues with the advisor supplying documentation rather than interpreting coverage. The honest framing throughout is that the advisor will press hard and prove the facts, but does not decide the result.

included: evidence assembly and proportionate claim construction
factual escalation through the supplier and relationship path
routing claims to the correct regime or process
honest expectation-setting about achievable remedy classes
excluded: interpreting insurance policy coverage or advising on a claim's merits
legal action or advice
promising or guaranteeing any compensation

pros.claim: A specific, evidenced and proportionate ask is answered far more often than an emotional complaint
pros.example: a claim citing the sold category, the confirmation and dated photographs, asking for the difference rather than for the trip to be made right

pros.claim: Visible advocacy after a failure is one of the strongest loyalty events available to an advisory practice, even when the recovery is partial
pros.example: a client who stays with the practice for years because of how a bad hotel was handled rather than because the trips were flawless

cons.claim: Pressing claims consumes unpaid hours and spends relationship capital that has other uses
cons.example: weeks of correspondence over a modest refund with an operator the practice books monthly

cons.claim: Clients often expect the advisor to deliver a remedy that the responsible party simply will not give, and the disappointment can land on the advisor
cons.example: a client who wanted the whole trip refunded for one poor night and reads a partial credit as the advisor failing

failure_modes: promising an outcome to calm a client and then failing to deliver it
filing a general complaint instead of a specific and evidenced ask
drifting into interpreting a protection policy's coverage for the client
letting the desire to protect a supplier relationship soften a legitimate claim
acceptance_tests: each claim on file names the specific failure, cites the sold-versus-delivered evidence, states a proportionate ask and records every response
no communication in the file promises a compensation outcome, and the achievable remedy classes were explained to the client in writing
revisit_triggers: a supplier refuses or ignores a documented claim
the same failure produces claims across multiple clients
a client escalates outside the practice

base.update_signal: claim outcomes cluster by supplier or by claim construction, showing which asks actually get answered

nodes.definition: The structured conversation after the client returns that harvests what actually happened and sorts it into the right bucket. The advisor asks specifically rather than generally - which base worked, which transfer was too tight, which guide was tired, what they would change, what surprised them - and then separates three different things that a happy or unhappy client will blend together: design error that belongs to the advisor, supplier failure that belongs to the ledger and possibly to a claim, and expectation mismatch that belongs to how the trip was described at proposal. Each finding is routed accordingly, so the design heuristics, the supplier record and the proposal language all improve from the same conversation. It is explicitly a quality-control instrument rather than a sales call: asking for a review, a referral or the next booking is a separate motion that happens later and belongs to the practice's client-retention discipline, not to this one.

included: specific structured questioning about the delivered trip
separating design error, supplier failure and expectation mismatch
routing each finding to design, ledger or proposal language
excluded: referral and review asks
anniversary or re-booking cadence and campaigns
valuing the client base

pros.claim: Sorting feedback into design, supplier and expectation buckets is what turns a pleasant chat into an improvement the next client can feel
pros.example: recognizing that a complaint about a rushed morning was a pacing decision by the advisor, not the operator's fault

pros.claim: A quality-first debrief that asks for nothing makes the later retention conversation easier because the client has already been heard
pros.example: a client who volunteers a recommendation unprompted because the debrief made clear the advisor wanted the truth

cons.claim: Clients soften negative feedback to be polite, so the debrief systematically under-reports problems unless questions are specific
cons.example: a party who says everything was lovely and mentions only in passing that they never used the second guide

cons.claim: Debriefs happen when the trip is over and the advisor is already working the next file, so they are the first thing dropped under pressure
cons.example: a busy season where three months of trips return with no debriefs recorded

failure_modes: asking how was the trip and accepting a one-word answer
recording feedback without attributing it to design, supplier or expectation
turning the debrief into a sales conversation and losing the honest answers
letting findings sit in notes without routing them anywhere
acceptance_tests: every completed trip has a debrief record, or an explicit note that the client declined one
each finding in the debrief is tagged as design, supplier or expectation and routed to the corresponding artifact
revisit_triggers: a client raises an issue after the debrief that the debrief did not surface
the same finding recurs across several trips
a supplier disputes a debrief finding attributed to them

base.update_signal: post-trip complaints arrive through other channels that the debrief should have caught, or debrief findings stop changing anything downstream

nodes.definition: The running, per-supplier record of delivered performance, kept as dated observations tied to specific bookings rather than as impressions. It tracks confirmation accuracy, whether what was sold is what arrived, on-the-ground quality and consistency, responsiveness when something broke and in whose time zone, honesty about problems rather than deflection, behavior on a redress claim, and payment and paperwork behavior toward the practice. Its purpose is to make future selection change on evidence: two documented failures on the same dimension should move a supplier down or off the shortlist regardless of how pleasant the relationship is, and a small operator that performed brilliantly under pressure should rise regardless of size. The ledger is the specific mechanism that stops a hosted lunch, a long friendship or a familiar brand from outweighing three bad client experiences.

included: dated per-booking performance observations
dimension-level tracking including disruption behavior and claim conduct
shortlist promotion and demotion rules driven by evidence
excluded: commission performance and payment amounts
supplier contract negotiation
public reviews or naming suppliers publicly

pros.claim: Dated, booking-linked evidence lets a supplier decision be defended to a client and to the advisor's own bias
pros.example: declining to recommend a familiar operator because the ledger shows three transfer failures in one season

pros.claim: The ledger converts scattered experience into a genuine practice asset that survives a bad memory or a busy season
pros.example: recalling instantly which of two similar operators actually answered during a strike two years ago

cons.claim: Small practices have thin per-supplier samples, so a single bad experience can unfairly condemn a good supplier
cons.example: one dreadful guide day recorded against an operator the practice has used only twice

cons.claim: Maintaining the ledger takes discipline at exactly the moment the trip is over and attention has moved on
cons.example: a season of trips whose observations were never written down and are now vague impressions

failure_modes: recording impressions rather than dated, booking-linked observations
letting relationship warmth override recorded failures
never demoting anyone, so the ledger accumulates without changing behavior
treating a single data point as a pattern
acceptance_tests: each entry names the booking, the date, the dimension and what was observed rather than a general rating
the shortlist used for selection reflects the ledger's current promotions and demotions
revisit_triggers: a supplier accumulates repeat failures on one dimension
a supplier changes ownership or key staff
a demoted supplier is proposed again for a specific client need

base.update_signal: accumulated entries change which supplier the practice would select for a repeat trip type, or a demoted supplier's new evidence contradicts the record

nodes.definition: Keeping the client record rich enough that the next trip starts from knowledge rather than from zero, while holding only what the work actually requires. The useful half is durable: preferences, pace, past bases and what they thought of them, celebration dates, loyalty numbers, seat and room habits, and the constraint history that makes a second design faster and better. The sensitive half is temporary: passport images and numbers, dates of birth, medical detail and any payment information are collected for a specific booking, held only as long as that booking needs them, protected under whatever data-protection obligation class applies in the practice's jurisdiction, and disposed of on a stated schedule rather than accumulating forever in an inbox. The steward's question is not whether something could be useful one day, but what would break if it leaked; the client's convenience is never a reason to keep an identity document longer than the booking requires.

included: durable preference and constraint history for future design
minimization, retention and disposal of sensitive identifiers
access discipline and protection appropriate to the practice's obligation class
excluded: legal advice on data-protection obligations, which must be verified against current rules in the jurisdiction
marketing consent management and campaign records
client-base valuation

pros.claim: A durable preference history is what makes a second trip feel effortless and is a genuine switching cost in the client's favor
pros.example: proposing a second itinerary that already accounts for the client's dislike of early flights and preference for a top-floor quiet room

pros.claim: Disposing of identity documents on schedule removes the practice's single largest breach exposure at no cost to service
pros.example: a compromised mailbox that contains no passport images because they were purged after each departure

cons.claim: Disposal costs convenience: the next booking has to ask for documents again, which clients experience as friction
cons.example: a repeat client irritated at re-sending passport details for the third trip in two years

cons.claim: Deciding what is durable versus sensitive requires judgment, and over-pruning loses context that made the practice valuable
cons.example: deleting the note explaining why a traveler cannot fly overnight along with the medical detail behind it

failure_modes: keeping passport images and card details indefinitely because they might be useful
storing sensitive detail in whatever channel it arrived in, including message threads
no retention schedule, so disposal never happens
treating a host's or supplier's system as covering an obligation the practice itself carries
acceptance_tests: sensitive identifiers have a stated retention period tied to the booking and evidence that disposal actually occurs
the durable client record contains preference and constraint history without carrying identity documents or payment data
the file names the data-protection obligation class the practice operates under and the date it was last verified
revisit_triggers: the practice changes systems, host or storage tooling
a data incident or near-miss occurs
the jurisdiction updates its data-protection requirement classes

base.update_signal: a data incident, a client access or deletion request, or a change in the jurisdiction's data-protection requirement classes

edges.why_related: the constraint map is built out of what the interview surfaced, and a constraint nobody asked about never enters it
entry obligations follow each traveler's passport and residency, which the map is where the practice records
the care protocol is triggered by documented circumstances rather than by impression, so it needs the map to know which travelers it applies to
the brief the client signs restates the band, its basis and the feasibility verdict, so it cannot be written before they exist
structural design is the first expensive labor and is only worth spending against a confirmed brief
a transit point or a country added for routing convenience can pull in a document class the party cannot satisfy, so the classes must be known before the routing is fixed
vetting is aimed at the candidates and the coverage gaps the map identifies rather than at suppliers at random
a supplier cannot be selected on fit before its terms, protection class and escalation path are known, since those are part of what the client is being sold
the fit rationale written for each component has to cite something in the signed brief, so the brief is the yardstick selection is measured against
program mechanics are applied only after the supplier has been chosen on fit, never as the reason it was chosen
the proposal presents the structural design and its trade-offs, so the skeleton with its buffers and anchors must exist first
the quote, the refundability picture and the compensation disclosure in the proposal all come out of which suppliers were selected and why
the accepted proposal is the reference the pre-commit check verifies category, dates and rate basis against
money moves only against a verified booking, and the merchant of record recorded at booking decides how the payment and any refund must be routed
the calendar is populated from the deadlines the booking step captured off the actual confirmation rather than from the supplier's general terms
reconciliation compares the arriving confirmation against the booking record the execution step wrote, so an unrecorded booking cannot be reconciled at all
documents are assembled from confirmations that have already been audited, otherwise the packet propagates the supplier's error to the traveler
the briefing walks the client through a packet they already hold, and confirming receipt is what makes that conversation possible
the routing rules and coverage limits agreed at briefing are what the disruption response executes against when something breaks
the escalation route used at two in the morning is an asset built in calm conditions and cannot be created during the incident
the timestamped incident log produced during the disruption is the evidence a later claim is built from
ledger entries are the debrief findings that were attributed to the supplier rather than to design or expectation
the band and its basis bound which bases, transport modes and guide days the structure can contain, and a design that ignores the band is unpresentable work
the care rules forbid the scarcity and urgency language a proposal close naturally reaches for, and require comprehension to be verified before a non-refundable commitment
alert lead times that are adequate for a habitual traveler are not adequate for a client who needs a companion in the conversation, so the care flag lengthens the notice the calendar must give
minimization bounds how much medical and identity detail the map may hold, so the map records the routing consequence rather than the underlying diagnosis wherever that is enough
the program pays and rewards the practice for routing volume to its properties, which is exactly the pull that fit-first selection exists to resist
edges.resolution_rule: fit against the signed brief decides the supplier; a program may only break a tie between options already judged equivalent on fit, and in every case the compensated relationship is disclosed in writing before the client decides - where compensation is the only differentiator, it is not a reason and both options go to the client visibly

edges.why_related: years of goodwill, hosted stays and a contact who always answers create a warmth toward a supplier that the recorded evidence of delivered failures contradicts
edges.resolution_rule: for future client selection the dated ledger evidence wins over relationship warmth; the relationship governs escalation and access only, and any hosted stay behind a recommendation is logged and disclosed

edges.why_related: buffers, minimum nights per base and internal flights that replace long drives all consume band the client would rather spend on more places and better rooms
edges.resolution_rule: buffers and daily loads that exist because of a documented constraint are not tradable; discretionary coverage, room category and optional experiences are cut first, and if the band still cannot carry the safe structure the feasibility verdict is reopened with the client rather than the buffers thinned

edges.why_related: an expiring hold or ticketing time limit pushes toward committing now, while the verification pass exists precisely to stop a commitment made in a hurry
edges.resolution_rule: verification wins: nothing is committed until names match the passport standard, dates, category and rate basis are checked against the accepted proposal - if the hold expires first, it expires and the space is requoted, because a reissue or name-change penalty and a denied boarding both cost more than a lost hold

edges.why_related: the interview wants to know everything about the traveler while stewardship wants the practice to hold as little sensitive material as the work allows
edges.resolution_rule: ask broadly but retain narrowly - preference, pace and constraint consequences are durable record, while identity documents, dates of birth, medical particulars and payment details are held only for the booking that needs them and disposed of on the stated schedule

edges.why_related: connection buffers, minimum nights and named anchor contingencies decide how often an ordinary delay becomes an incident the advisor has to work, so design choices cause the in-trip workload
a claim succeeds on the documented gap between what was sold and what was confirmed, so the presence or absence of a reconciliation record causes the claim to be provable or merely asserted

the specificity of the success criteria captured at discovery determines whether a disappointment can be attributed to design, supplier or expectation, because there is nothing to attribute it against otherwise
deposit and final payment actions are fired by calendar entries and then executed through the payment route recorded for that supplier, in that order
the claim is opened while the evidence is fresh and the debrief follows once the client is home, so the debrief can record what remedy was actually available rather than what was hoped for
promotions and demotions recorded after delivered trips change the shortlist the next fit decision is made from, which is the only mechanism that makes the ledger worth keeping
findings tagged as design error rather than supplier failure revise the practice's pacing, buffer and minimum-night heuristics for the next client
demoting the only mapped option for a destination converts a supplier problem into a coverage gap the map must record and the practice must fill or decline

both are dated-verification disciplines with the same failure shape - trusting memory or last season's terms instead of re-reading the current source, and treating a check made at booking as still true at departure

conflict_axes.name: client_fit_versus_compensated_preference
conflict_axes.description: Preferred programs, consortium partnerships and host arrangements pay the practice for routing volume, while the client is buying a recommendation they believe was made for them; the tension is permanent because both pulls are real and the compensated option is often genuinely good.
poles: book the supplier that best serves the signed brief
book the supplier that compensates the practice better
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: fit decides, compensation may only tie-break genuine equivalence, and the relationship is disclosed in writing before the client decides rather than after they ask

conflict_axes.name: trip_ambition_versus_documented_capability
conflict_axes.description: Clients ask for the itinerary their friends did or the one they could have done ten years ago, while the constraint map records what this party can actually sustain; deferring to the client sells a trip that fails on day three, and overriding them slides into age or ability assumption.
poles: design the trip the client is asking for
design the trip the recorded constraints support
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the conversation against documented facts rather than impressions, restate the physical reality of each day in plain terms, let a competent adult accept a risk they understand, and decline only what the practice genuinely cannot deliver safely

conflict_axes.name: commitment_speed_versus_verification
conflict_axes.description: Live inventory, expiring holds and ticketing time limits reward speed, while every expensive error in the practice is made in the last two minutes before a commit; the pressure is worst on exactly the bookings that matter most.
poles: commit before the space or fare disappears
verify every field before anything is committed
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the verification pass is never skipped, only compressed where the underlying data is already on file; a released hold is requoted, while a wrong name on an issued ticket is a penalty or a denied boarding

conflict_axes.name: coverage_versus_pacing_and_buffers
conflict_axes.description: Clients often measure a trip by how much of the destination it contains, while durable satisfaction comes from minimum nights per base, real arrival days and connection buffers that absorb the ordinary failures of travel.
poles: fit in more places and more sights
protect pace, buffers and unplanned time
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: show the trade explicitly in the proposal with the specific risk each removed buffer creates, keep constraint-driven pacing non-negotiable, and let the client spend discretionary slack knowingly

conflict_axes.name: price_transparency_versus_conversion
conflict_axes.description: Volunteering that a component is available directly, naming the refundability ladder and stating how the practice is compensated all make the client better informed and some of them slower or unwilling to book.
poles: disclose everything before the decision
present only what is needed to decide
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: disclosure is not optional, so the answer is to pair every disclosure with what the difference buys - the program benefits, the terms, the advocate when it breaks - and to accept the bookings lost to a self-service channel as the cost of an advisory relationship

conflict_axes.name: client_convenience_versus_funds_and_data_discipline
conflict_axes.description: Clients want one payment, stored cards and passport details kept on file forever, while every one of those conveniences moves money or identity documents into the practice and raises a requirement class or a breach exposure the practice must carry.
poles: make paying and re-booking effortless for the client
keep client money and identity documents out of the practice
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: supplier as merchant of record and per-booking retention are the defaults; any consolidated collection is blocked until the client-funds requirement class is verified as current in the operating jurisdiction, and the friction of re-collecting documents is explained as protection rather than apologized for

conflict_axes.name: supplier_relationship_versus_client_advocacy
conflict_axes.description: The contact who rescues a stranded client is the same person a firm claim is filed against, and a practice that presses every claim hard eventually finds the escalation line slower to answer.
poles: protect the relationship that rescues clients
press the claim the client is owed
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep claims factual, specific and proportionate rather than emotional, escalate on evidence rather than volume, and never soften a legitimate claim to protect access - a supplier that punishes an evidenced claim is a ledger entry in itself

conflict_axes.name: availability_promise_versus_sustainable_practice
conflict_axes.description: Round-the-clock support is what clients want to hear and what competitors advertise, while a one-person practice sleeping in another time zone cannot staff it; the gap surfaces at the worst possible moment.
poles: promise constant availability to win the client
state honestly what coverage exists and who covers the gap
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: state reachability, response windows and the cover arrangement at briefing in writing, route ground-level problems to the supplier who can actually solve them, and keep a stated update cadence during incidents so honesty does not read as absence

conflict_axes.name: design_depth_versus_scope_lock
conflict_axes.description: The interviewing and structural work that make the trip worth buying are unpaid until something is booked, while the brief and revision-round limits that protect those hours can make a warm relationship feel transactional too early.
poles: give generously to earn the relationship
lock scope before spending design hours
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep discovery generous and unbounded, put the scope lock at the point where structural design begins, and size the formality to the trip so a four-night repeat booking does not carry the paperwork of a three-week custom itinerary

conflict_axes.name: certainty_clients_want_versus_what_can_be_promised
conflict_axes.description: Clients want to hear that entry is assured, the upgrade is confirmed and the refund will come through, while every one of those outcomes is decided by a border officer, a front desk or a supplier's claims department that the advisor does not control.
poles: give the client the reassurance they are asking for
state only what the practice can actually stand behind
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: separate what the advisor does from what the advisor achieves - the requirement class was verified on a dated source, the benefit is confirmed on the reservation and delivered at the property's discretion, the claim will be evidenced and pressed but the remedy is the supplier's decision

edge_cases.description: A traveler books under a married surname while her passport still shows her maiden name, and the mismatch surfaces only after the air segment has been ticketed
edge_cases.trigger: a name is taken from an email signature, a payment card or a previous file rather than from the passport itself
edge_cases.mitigation: require a passport image or a written passport-standard name confirmation per traveler before any ticketing or non-refundable commit, and treat a name correction as an immediate supplier escalation within any free-correction window rather than a task for later

edge_cases.description: A traveler discloses a new mobility limitation or a scheduled operation after final payment, when the itinerary is fully committed and the penalty ladder has reached its steepest step
edge_cases.trigger: a health change occurs between sign-off and departure and the client does not think to mention it until the pre-departure conversation
edge_cases.mitigation: re-confirm the constraint map in writing before final payment and again at briefing, then separate what can still be changed at no cost from what carries a penalty and put both to the client plainly before anything is altered

edge_cases.description: A vetted operator ceases trading between deposit and departure, with client money already paid and the trip weeks away
edge_cases.trigger: a supplier failure that clean diligence did not predict, which no amount of vetting can eliminate
edge_cases.mitigation: read off the file how the client's funds were held and which protection-scheme class applied to that booking, route the client to the card-issuer or scheme process that fits how the money actually moved, rebuild the affected components from the vetted alternatives, and tell the client honestly what is recoverable and by whom rather than promising recovery

edge_cases.description: An airline schedule change arrives inside a reissued confirmation, silently retiming the arrival and breaking two prepaid ground transfers and a first-night hotel
edge_cases.trigger: a supplier-initiated amendment that is pushed as a document rather than announced as a change
edge_cases.mitigation: audit every reissued document against the booking record on the day it arrives, trace each changed time through the dependent components rather than only fixing the flight, and issue a dated addendum with confirmed receipt if documents are already with the client

edge_cases.description: An adult child takes over the conversation and directs the booking for an elderly parent who is present, competent and quietly disagreeing
edge_cases.trigger: a family member joins the process as an organizer and begins answering on the traveler's behalf
edge_cases.mitigation: confirm with the traveling client directly who is authorized to decide, address decisions to that person and record their own words, welcome the family member as support rather than as principal, and record the comprehension check with the traveler rather than with the organizer

edge_cases.description: A client has found a villa or small operator online, wants a deposit sent today to hold it, and reads the vetting delay as the advisor being slow
edge_cases.trigger: client-sourced inventory arriving with its own deadline and no diligence behind it
edge_cases.mitigation: state plainly what has not yet been checked and what that exposes, run the minimum diligence set of identity, contract terms, who holds the money and an escalation contact before any payment, and if the client proceeds regardless, record in writing that the booking was client-directed and unvetted

edge_cases.description: An entry authorization or health-declaration class is introduced for a booked destination after the deposit was taken
edge_cases.trigger: an official source publishes a new requirement class between booking and departure
edge_cases.mitigation: re-verify per passport against the current official source, notify every traveler in writing with the date checked and the official channel to use, keep the dated record showing the requirement did not exist at the earlier check, and re-check again in the pre-departure window without interpreting eligibility for anyone

edge_cases.description: Fifteen households on a family reunion want to send one payment to the advisor rather than each paying four suppliers
edge_cases.trigger: a group or multi-household booking where consolidation is the obvious convenience
edge_cases.mitigation: treat any pass-through of client funds as triggering client-funds, trust-account or seller-of-travel requirement classes that must be verified as current in the operating jurisdiction before it is used at all, and default instead to per-household payment direct to each supplier with the calendar carrying the collection dates

edge_cases.description: The only supplier that can deliver the trip in a remote region is one the performance ledger has already demoted
edge_cases.trigger: a client request that lands squarely in a coverage gap created by a demotion
edge_cases.mitigation: vet an alternative rather than quietly reinstating the demoted supplier; if none exists, put the specific documented failures to the client, restructure to reduce exposure to the weak dimension, or decline the trip honestly rather than sending a client into a known problem

edge_cases.description: An overnight flight arrives the following calendar day, so the hotel booked for the departure date sits empty while the party arrives to a room that starts a night late
edge_cases.trigger: a date-line or red-eye routing where the travel date and the arrival date differ
edge_cases.mitigation: check hotel check-in against the arrival date rather than the departure date at the pre-commit pass, and make the arrival-day buffer in the skeleton carry the explicit arrival date so reconciliation has an unambiguous reference to audit against

edge_cases.description: A client is stranded overnight and the named escalation contact has left the supplier, with the general service line quoting policy and nothing else
edge_cases.trigger: a live incident that reveals relationship records went stale since they were last needed
edge_cases.mitigation: work the supplier's own channel to exhaustion while keeping the stated update cadence to the client, establish which party contractually owns the fix before buying anything, log every name and time, and refresh the escalation record for that supplier immediately after the incident closes

edge_cases.description: A repeat client asks the practice to keep passport images and card details on file permanently so future bookings are effortless
edge_cases.trigger: a convenience request from a valued client that runs directly against retention discipline
edge_cases.mitigation: explain that identity documents and payment details are held only for the booking that needs them and disposed of on schedule, keep the durable preference history that actually makes the next trip faster, and route card details through the supplier or host secure channel every time rather than storing them for reuse

workflow.action: Interview the client rather than take the order
workflow.description: Run the structured conversation that surfaces party and decision structure, past-trip stories, sustainable pace, the occasion, non-negotiables and the client's own words for success, and write it down as it is said
workflow.artifact: written discovery record in the client's own language
workflow.gate: every traveler is named, the decision-maker and any veto-holder are identified, at least one past-trip story with what worked and what failed is recorded, and the client's own success sentence is quoted

workflow.description: Record for each individual the mobility, stamina, dietary and routing-relevant medical facts, passport nationality and residency, hard date constraints and rooming dynamics, with a date and an attribution on every entry
workflow.gate: every traveler has an individual line or an explicit none-disclosed marker, each entry carries a date and who disclosed it, and no sensitive detail is held that the booking and routing do not require

workflow.action: Verify entry-document requirement classes per passport and per segment
workflow.description: Identify which validity, visa, authorization, transit, onward-ticket, health and minor-consent classes apply to each traveler on this routing, verify each against the current official source, and put the result in writing with the date checked
workflow.artifact: dated entry-document verification sheet with sources named
workflow.gate: each traveler has a dated line per country entered or transited naming the class and the official source consulted, and the client has acknowledged in writing that holding valid documents remains the traveler's own responsibility

workflow.action: Frame the budget basis and issue the feasibility verdict
workflow.description: Settle whether the band is per person or per party, land-only or all-in, air in or out, explain the cost drivers as mechanisms, and say honestly whether the requested trip exists at that band on those dates with this lead time
workflow.artifact: written budget band with its basis, its exclusions and a feasibility verdict
workflow.gate: the band states its basis and what it explicitly does not buy, and a dates-and-lead-time verdict is on file before any design labor begins

workflow.action: Get the trip brief confirmed in writing
workflow.description: Restate party, dates and their real flexibility, band and basis, constraint summary, must-haves, must-avoids, what is out of scope, how many revision rounds the design includes and what the client must supply, then obtain confirmation
workflow.artifact: client-confirmed trip design brief, dated and versioned
workflow.gate: the client's written confirmation is on file before structural design starts, and the brief contains an explicit not-included list and a stated number of revision rounds

workflow.action: Vet every supplier the trip will touch before it is presented
workflow.description: For each candidate, establish identity and history, how client funds are held and which protection-scheme class applies to this booking in this jurisdiction, the cancellation ladder and force-majeure, schedule-change and name-change terms, the merchant of record, and a named human escalation contact
workflow.artifact: per-supplier vetting file with terms, protection class and escalation contact
workflow.gate: no supplier reaches a client proposal until its penalty ladder, change terms, merchant-of-record identity, applicable protection-scheme class and named escalation contact are on file

workflow.description: Sequence the geography, set minimum nights per base, build a real arrival day, size transfer and connection buffers to each segment's actual risk, place date-fixed anchors with named contingencies, and match daily walking, driving and altitude loads to the constraint map
workflow.artifact: day-by-day structural skeleton with buffers, loads and anchors visible
workflow.gate: the arrival buffer and minimum-night rule are respected, every date-fixed anchor has a named contingency, and each day's load has been checked line by line against the constraint map

workflow.action: Select each component on fit and disclose the compensated relationships
workflow.description: Choose the supplier for each component against the signed brief, write the one-line fit rationale citing what the client actually said, and state in plain language any preferred, consortium, host or hosted-stay relationship behind the recommendation
workflow.artifact: component selection sheet with a fit rationale and a disclosure line per component
workflow.gate: every component cites a specific brief item as its reason, a dated written disclosure of any compensated relationship is prepared for the client, and no component stands on compensation as its only differentiator

workflow.action: Present the proposal as a decision meeting
workflow.description: Lead with one recommendation and its reason in the client's words, offer a small bounded set of alternatives, compose the quote transparently with inclusions, exclusions and refundability, state honestly where a component could be bought elsewhere and how the practice is paid, then close on a named next step
workflow.artifact: proposal document plus a recorded decision conversation with objections captured
workflow.gate: inclusions, exclusions and per-component refundability are in plain language, the compensation and online-comparison statements are on file, no scarcity or fear language is used as the reason to decide, and a specific next step and date are agreed

workflow.action: Execute the bookings behind a pre-commit verification pass
workflow.description: Immediately before each deposit, ticket issue or non-refundable action, verify names to the passport standard, dates including overnight arrivals, category and bedding, and the exact rate or fare basis against the accepted proposal, then book through the channel carrying the intended terms and route the payment to the supplier as merchant of record
workflow.artifact: booking register holding locators, exact rate basis, terms, payment log and every supplier deadline
workflow.gate: the second-pass check is recorded for every commit, the locator and rate basis are captured on the day, every payment names its merchant of record, and each component's deadline classes and penalty-ladder steps are entered with owner and alert lead time

workflow.description: Audit each arriving confirmation against the accepted proposal on the day it lands, then assemble a packet a tired traveler can use - locators, day-by-day with usable addresses, transfer instructions with a fallback, supplier and emergency contacts and the practice's escalation instructions - deliver it, confirm receipt and walk it through at the pre-departure briefing
workflow.artifact: reconciliation notes, delivered document packet with confirmed receipt, and a recorded pre-departure briefing
workflow.gate: every confirmation carries a dated reconciliation note, receipt of the packet is confirmed in writing, the coverage and escalation routing given to the client is recorded, and the final entry-document re-check is on file

workflow.action: Debrief the delivered trip and route what it taught
workflow.description: Ask specifically about bases, transfers, guides and pace, separate design error from supplier failure from expectation mismatch, route each finding to the design heuristics, the supplier ledger or the proposal language, and close the file down to what may be retained
workflow.artifact: debrief record with tagged findings, updated supplier ledger entries and a disposal note for sensitive identifiers
workflow.gate: every completed trip has a debrief or a recorded decline, each finding is tagged and routed, ledger entries name the booking and the dimension observed, and identity documents and payment details for the completed booking have been disposed of on schedule

dominance_rules.rule: Traveler safety and documented capability dominate itinerary ambition and any sale
dominance_rules.rationale: a trip that exceeds what a traveler can sustain fails in the destination, where nothing can be fixed and the harm is physical rather than commercial
dominance_rules.trigger: a requested element exceeds a limitation recorded in the constraint map, or a traveler asks for an itinerary their disclosed condition does not support
dominance_rules.action: restate the physical reality of the day in plain terms, redesign to what the record supports, and decline the element rather than sell it if the gap cannot be closed

dominance_rules.rule: Fit against the signed brief dominates what the practice earns from a supplier
dominance_rules.rationale: the entire value of an advisory relationship rests on the client believing the recommendation was made for them, and one hidden steer destroys it permanently
dominance_rules.trigger: two suppliers can deliver a component and one compensates the practice better
dominance_rules.action: book on fit, use compensation only to break a genuine tie, and if compensation is the only differentiator hand both options to the client with the difference visible

dominance_rules.rationale: a client cannot weigh a recommendation they do not know is compensated, and disclosure discovered later is indistinguishable from concealment
dominance_rules.trigger: any recommendation involving a preferred program, consortium arrangement, host relationship, override or a hosted stay the advisor has received
dominance_rules.action: state the relationship in plain language in writing before the client decides, never in a footnote or a link, even at the cost of the booking

dominance_rules.rule: The pre-commit verification pass dominates hold and inventory pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: a released hold is requoted while a wrong name on an issued ticket, a wrong date or the wrong rate basis carries penalties, denied boarding or a trip that does not match what was sold
dominance_rules.trigger: a hold, option or ticketing time limit expires before verification data is complete
dominance_rules.action: let the hold lapse and requote rather than commit unverified, and never plan to correct after the fact

dominance_rules.rule: Verification against the current official source dominates memory, peer forums and last year's trip
dominance_rules.rationale: entry, transit and health requirement classes change without notice and per nationality, so any recollection is evidence of nothing
dominance_rules.trigger: any entry-document, transit or health question arising at design, at booking or before departure
dominance_rules.action: check the current official source per passport, record the class, the source and the date, notify the client in writing, and re-check in the pre-departure window

dominance_rules.rule: Supplier as merchant of record dominates client payment convenience
dominance_rules.rationale: keeping the practice out of the money chain preserves the client's own dispute rights and avoids requirement classes a small practice may not be authorized to carry
dominance_rules.trigger: any request to consolidate payments, hold a deposit at the agency or collect group funds
dominance_rules.action: default to direct-to-supplier payment, and block any pass-through until the client-funds or seller-of-travel requirement class has been verified as current in the operating jurisdiction

dominance_rules.rule: Dated ledger evidence dominates relationship warmth in future supplier selection
dominance_rules.rationale: hospitality, friendship and brand familiarity are exactly the biases that make an advisor keep sending clients to a supplier that has already failed them
dominance_rules.trigger: a supplier with recorded failures on a dimension is being considered for a booking that depends on that dimension
dominance_rules.action: select from the ledger's current shortlist, and if the demoted supplier is the only option put its documented failures to the client rather than reinstating it quietly

dominance_rules.rule: Establishing the contractual owner of the fix dominates advisor improvisation during a disruption
dominance_rules.rationale: buying replacement services before the responsible party has been made to perform spends the client's money on something they were already owed and can extinguish a better remedy
dominance_rules.trigger: a live disruption where the traveler is safe and a commercial fix is being considered
dominance_rules.action: identify which party owes the fix, tell the traveler what to avoid accepting until that is clear, work the supplier's own channel first, and only then consider buying an alternative

dominance_rules.rule: The no-fear-selling rule dominates genuine scarcity
dominance_rules.rationale: urgency is corrosive even when it is true, because a client who commits under pressure cannot be said to have understood what they committed to
dominance_rules.trigger: real inventory or price pressure exists and would move the client to decide now
dominance_rules.action: state the fact and the date neutrally, give the client the exposure in plain terms, and let the space go rather than close on fear

dominance_rules.rule: The signed brief dominates recollection in any dispute about what was included
dominance_rules.rationale: bespoke work drifts, and a versioned document both sides confirmed is the only defense against two honest but incompatible memories
dominance_rules.trigger: a disagreement about scope, inclusions, revision rounds or what the client was promised
dominance_rules.action: resolve against the confirmed brief, and record any accepted change as a new version rather than absorbing it silently

dominance_rules.rule: Data minimization dominates future convenience for sensitive identifiers
dominance_rules.rationale: the correct question is not whether a document might be useful again but what would break if it leaked, and a small practice cannot absorb an identity-document breach
dominance_rules.trigger: a decision about retaining passport images, dates of birth, medical particulars or payment details after a booking is complete
dominance_rules.action: keep the durable preference and constraint history, dispose of identity and payment material on the stated schedule, and re-collect it for the next booking

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build the per-traveler constraint map before designing a single day
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the full structural redesign that follows when a party-level assumption meets an individual's real limit, which arrives after the skeleton, the quotes and sometimes the deposit

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify entry-document requirement classes per passport before the routing is fixed or quoted
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rebuilding a routing because a transit point pulled in an authorization class a traveler cannot satisfy, and the denied-boarding exposure that follows if it is never caught

anti_rework_rules.rule: Settle the budget basis and issue the feasibility verdict before any design labor
anti_rework_rules.prevents: designing at length against a number that meant something else, or against dates on which the trip does not exist, and then doing the whole design again

anti_rework_rules.rule: Obtain written brief sign-off before structural design starts
anti_rework_rules.prevents: scope creep absorbed silently as unpaid revision rounds and the argument at proposal about what was always included

anti_rework_rules.rule: Vet a supplier and read its penalty ladder before it appears in a client proposal
anti_rework_rules.prevents: withdrawing a recommendation the client has already fallen in love with, and discovering unacceptable payment or cancellation terms after a deposit is due

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the fit rationale and the compensation disclosure at the moment of selection, not at proposal time
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reconstructing a justification under pressure when a client asks why this supplier, and the quiet drift toward the preferred list as the default shortlist

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the passport-standard name, date, category and rate-basis check before every commit
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reissue and name-change penalties, a hotel night lost to an overnight arrival, and a rate that matched on price but not on the terms that were quoted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Capture the record locator, the exact rate basis and every supplier deadline on the day of booking
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-contacting suppliers to reconstruct a booking in order to service a change, and missing a penalty-ladder step nobody wrote down

anti_rework_rules.rule: Reconcile each confirmation against the accepted proposal on the day it arrives
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a substitution or schedule change discovered by the traveler at a check-in desk, when it is no longer free to fix and has become a service failure

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm receipt of the document packet and of every addendum in writing before departure
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a traveler arriving with no documents or carrying a superseded version, and the avoidable arrival incident that follows

anti_rework_rules.rule: Log disruption actions, names and times as they happen rather than reconstructing afterwards
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unprovable claim, where the practice knows what went wrong but cannot evidence it and the client absorbs a loss they were owed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every debrief finding as design, supplier or expectation before filing it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: untagged feedback that changes nothing, so the same pacing error or the same weak operator is sold to the next client

iteration_protocol.trigger: a traveler discloses or corrects a constraint after the brief was signed
iteration_protocol.action: reopen the constraint map, then re-check the daily loads, the entry-document classes and the penalty exposure that rest on it, and put what can still be changed at no cost and what now carries a penalty to the client before altering anything

iteration_protocol.trigger: a supplier issues a schedule change, substitution or reissued document
iteration_protocol.action: re-reconcile the affected confirmation against the accepted proposal, trace the change through every dependent component and buffer, and issue a dated addendum with confirmed receipt if documents are already with the client

iteration_protocol.trigger: an official source changes an entry, transit or health requirement class for a booked destination
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify per passport against the current official source, notify each traveler in writing with the date checked and the official channel, and keep the earlier dated record showing what the requirement was when it was last checked

iteration_protocol.trigger: a deadline is missed or only met by hours
iteration_protocol.action: reopen the deadline classes being tracked and the alert lead times behind them, and check whether the miss came from a class nobody was tracking or from a reminder that fired too late for a human to act

iteration_protocol.trigger: the operating jurisdiction updates client-funds, card-handling, seller-of-travel or data-protection requirement classes
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify which classes now apply to the practice, adjust payment routing and retention accordingly, and record the date and the source consulted rather than relying on what a host or supplier says covers it

iteration_protocol.trigger: a client asks why a supplier was recommended, or a compensated relationship the practice holds changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-audit the fit rationales on the open bookings for brief citations that actually exist, refresh the disclosure language, and re-check that no live recommendation stands on compensation as its only differentiator

iteration_protocol.trigger: a live escalation fails or a named supplier contact leaves
iteration_protocol.action: refresh the escalation record for that supplier, test the replacement route while nothing is broken, and record what the failed route cost during the incident

iteration_protocol.trigger: a supplier accumulates repeat documented failures on the same dimension
iteration_protocol.action: demote it in the ledger, rebuild the shortlist for the trip types that depended on it, and record the resulting coverage gap in the supplier map so it is filled deliberately rather than discovered at the next enquiry

iteration_protocol.trigger: the same debrief finding recurs across several trips
iteration_protocol.action: treat it as a systemic fault rather than an incident and route it to whichever artifact owns it, revising the pacing and buffer heuristics, the supplier shortlist or the proposal language that set the expectation

priority_rationale: Intake comes first because everything downstream is checked against it: the discovery record defines what the trip is for, the per-traveler constraint map bounds what can be designed, the entry-document classes decide what routings are even available to these passports, and the budget band plus feasibility verdict decide whether the trip exists at all - all four precede the signed brief that licenses expensive design labor. Supplier vetting runs alongside intake rather than after it, because a supplier's terms, protection class and escalation contact are part of what the client is being sold and must be known before any recommendation is made. Design and selection follow the brief, with fit-first choice and its written disclosure gating the proposal, so no client ever decides on a recommendation whose compensation they have not been told about. Execution then dominates: the pre-commit verification pass, the payment route, the deadline calendar and the confirmation audit are ordered so that every irreversible act happens after its check rather than before it. Delivery, briefing, disruption response and redress rest on the records those earlier steps produced, and the quality loop - debrief, supplier ledger and a client file pruned to what may be retained - comes last because it is the only part that improves the next trip rather than this one.
